clue.text: Retail decision made — I'm extending credit

definitions.meaning: what a shopper says on deciding to purchase an item
what a listener says on deciding to believe a story, giving it credence

explanation.walkthrough: 'Credit' looks financial, which ties in with the shop, but here it means belief: the phrase is also said when accepting someone's claim.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is both a purchaser's verdict at the till and an idiom for accepting someone's account as true.

clue.text: Become responsible for terminal, and able to depart

indicators.note: to depart means the word able leaves the synonym for terminal

parts.note: a terminal illness is incurable

explanation.surface: Someone takes on responsibility for an airport terminal and is free to leave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terminal' suggests an airport but means fatal, INCURABLE; 'and able to depart' then removes ABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: To incur a debt or penalty is to become liable for it.

clue.text: Perhaps one held up to ridicule at last calmer after explosion

indicators.note: after explosion means the letters are blown apart and reassembled
at last means the final letter of the word ridicule is taken

explanation.surface: Someone mocked in public finally grows calmer after an outburst.
explanation.walkthrough: TO + E (end of 'ridicule') + CALMER are rearranged together. 'held up' means delayed, not mocked.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone delayed, held up by traffic for example, arrives late and becomes a latecomer.

clue.text: Strange — millions gifted to firm

parts.note: unco is a Scots word for strange or unusual
M is the abbreviation for million(s)
a promising player is talented, gifted

explanation.surface: Oddly, a fortune was given away to a company.
explanation.walkthrough: UNCO is Scots for strange. 'firm' looks like a company but is an adjective: unbending.
explanation.definitionFit: An uncompromising stance is firm and unwilling to yield.

clue.text: Hero's academic works captivated university

indicators.note: captivated means the academic works hold the university letter captive inside

parts.note: theses are academic dissertations

explanation.surface: A hero's scholarly writing charmed a whole university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'captivated' puts U inside THESES.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek mythical hero who killed the Minotaur in the Cretan labyrinth.

clue.text: A tot in short queue for kids' show

indicators.note: in means the word for tot is placed inside the shortened queue
short means the last letter of the word for queue is dropped

parts.note: a queue is a line
to tot up is to add

explanation.surface: A toddler waits in a brief queue for a children's performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tot' looks like a small child, but here it is the verb meaning to sum up; 'short' trims the queue word before the sum goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: A favourite British Christmas pantomime, a stage show for children, based on the tale of the lamp.

clue.text: Fine political party that's often fought

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencil leads
Lab is the short form of the UK Labour Party

explanation.surface: A small political party with a good record keeps getting into battles.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the vaguest part of the clue: excess body fat is something dieters constantly battle against.
explanation.definitionFit: Excess body fat is the thing slimmers wage a continual battle against.

clue.text: Spread out neatly in gift boxes

indicators.note: boxes means the words neatly in gift enclose the answer within them

explanation.surface: Something is spread out neatly inside gift boxes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boxes' looks like a noun, but it is a verb: the words hold the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something lying is stretched out flat, reclining.

clue.text: Wretched people come to a district in Ireland

parts.note: bally is a dated euphemism for bloody, i.e. wretched
men are people

explanation.surface: Miserable folk arrive at an Irish district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bally' is old British slang standing in for the swear word bloody.
explanation.definitionFit: Ballymena is a town and former district council area in County Antrim, Northern Ireland.

clue.text: Silly fuss damages important cause

indicators.note: damages means the letters of important cause are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A trivial row harms a serious campaign.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for a great fuss over something trivial.

clue.text: Chop I wash, removing an area of dead skin

parts.note: to chop is to cut

indicators.note: removing tells us the word an is taken out of the synonym for wash

parts.note: to wash something is to clean it
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone describes cutting and scrubbing at a patch of dead skin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'removing' takes AN out of CLEAN, leaving CLE.
explanation.definitionFit: The cuticle is the strip of hardened dead skin at the base of a fingernail or toenail.

clue.text: The last in a series of disasters that's left by building workers

indicators.note: in tells us the piece for the last sits inside the other two pieces

parts.note: taken as written
ill as a noun means misfortune or disaster
nth means the last or latest in a long sequence, as in 'for the nth time'

explanation.surface: A tale of catastrophe ends with something abandoned by construction workers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Building workers' looks like builders, but it means ants, which build mounds of earth; the clue's 'in' wraps the first pieces round the last.
explanation.definitionFit: Ants are the workers who build the mound of earth they leave behind as their nest.

clue.text: Advise leftie to keep remark short

indicators.note: to keep means the word for leftie holds the other piece inside it

parts.note: a Red is a left-winger

indicators.note: short means the last letter of the word for remark is cut off

parts.note: a remark is a comment

explanation.surface: Someone tells a left-wing colleague to keep their comments brief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leftie' sounds like a left-handed person, but it is the political sense: a communist or socialist.
explanation.definitionFit: To recommend a course of action is to advise someone to take it.

clue.text: In town, the carpet-maker is …

parts.note: a carpet is a rug, and who made it is given by 'by'; together they name an English town

explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis invites a completion: the carpet would be labelled 'rug by' its maker. Rugby is a market town in Warwickshire, England, home of the school where the sport began.
explanation.definitionFit: The town is named literally by the label a rug would carry naming who made it.

clue.text: Old civilisation the founder of another backed

indicators.note: backed means the founder's name is read from end to start

parts.note: Remus was, with Romulus, a legendary founder of Rome, another old civilisation

explanation.surface: An ancient culture was supported by the man who founded a rival one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backed' looks like support, but it turns REMUS round.
explanation.definitionFit: Sumer was the ancient civilisation of southern Mesopotamia, among the earliest known.

clue.text: Classical versifier filled parts of feet with power — this in Latin

indicators.note: filled means the parts of feet contain the other pieces

parts.note: soles are the undersides of the feet
hoc is the Latin for this

explanation.surface: An ancient poet packed metrical feet with force, as the Latin has it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'feet' suggests verse metre, matching the poet, but means the body part.
explanation.definitionFit: Sophocles was an ancient Greek tragic playwright, whose plays are in verse.

clue.text: Extremely silly show without initial backers

indicators.note: extremely means the first and last letters of the word silly are taken
without initial means the first letter of the word for show is dropped

parts.note: to show something is to indicate it

explanation.surface: A ridiculous programme goes ahead with no starting investors.
explanation.walkthrough: The held text had a stray S after 'without'; the page prints none. 'show' looks like a noun (a programme) but is the verb, point out.
explanation.definitionFit: A syndicate is a group of investors who jointly back a venture.

clue.text: Clear-out opening space to display Raphael, say

indicators.note: opening space to means the scrambled letters part to let another word in
out means the letters of clear are put out of order

parts.note: to hang paintings is to display them

explanation.surface: A gallery clear-out makes room to exhibit a Raphael painting.
explanation.walkthrough: CLEAR rearranged as ARCEL opens to take HANG: ARC-HANG-EL. 'Raphael' suggests the painter, but it is the angel.
explanation.definitionFit: Raphael is one of the archangels named in scripture and tradition.

clue.text: Epic drama involved emergency worker

indicators.note: involved means the letters of epic drama are tangled together into a new order

explanation.surface: A grand theatrical production features someone from the ambulance service.
explanation.walkthrough: The held text had a stray V before 'worker'; the page prints none.
explanation.definitionFit: A paramedic is a trained ambulance worker who gives emergency medical care.

clue.text: Disaster as class make up for time lost in discussion

indicators.note: make up for means the class letters stand in place of the time letter

parts.note: a debate is a formal discussion
CL is the abbreviation for class

explanation.surface: A calamity as pupils catch up on time wasted in talk.
explanation.walkthrough: In DEBATE the T ('time lost') is replaced by CL.
explanation.definitionFit: A debacle is a sudden, humiliating collapse or fiasco.

clue.text: Dog taking up colourful soup

parts.note: a chow is a Chinese breed of dog

indicators.note: taking up means the colour word is read upwards in this down answer

parts.note: red is a colour, so colourful hints at red

explanation.surface: A dog takes to a vivid soup.
explanation.definitionFit: Chowder is a thick soup, usually of fish or clams.

clue.text: Discharge about to be reversed? Capital!

indicators.note: to be reversed means the two pieces together are read backwards

parts.note: an arc is an electrical discharge between two points
ca is short for circa, meaning about

explanation.surface: A question about turning back a discharge, answered with an exclamation of approval.
explanation.walkthrough: ARC + CA backwards gives ACCRA. 'Capital!' looks like an old-fashioned exclamation meaning excellent, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Accra is the capital city of Ghana.

clue.text: Cursing, catching horse with crop

indicators.note: catching means the crop word holds the other letter inside it

parts.note: oats are a cereal crop
H is slang for heroin, which is also called horse

explanation.surface: Someone swears while trying to catch a horse with a riding crop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'horse' is drug slang for heroin, abbreviated H. 'crop' suggests a riding whip but is the farm sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Oaths are swear words, so cursing is a stream of them.

clue.text: In a series of races champion has no part to play

indicators.note: In at the front means the champion goes inside the races

parts.note: the TT is the Isle of Man motorcycle races
an ace is a champion

explanation.surface: A champion in a run of races is left without a role.
explanation.walkthrough: The TT (Tourist Trophy) is a series of motorcycle races on the Isle of Man.
explanation.definitionFit: Tacet in a musical score tells a player to stay silent for a movement.

clue.text: React badly to sugary confection, say — it keeps coming back

parts.note: an audience that reacts badly may boo

indicators.note: say tells us we want something that sounds like the sweet, not its spelling

parts.note: a meringue is a confection of whipped egg white and sugar

explanation.surface: Someone recoils from a sweet pudding that repeats on them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it keeps coming back' sounds like a dish that repeats, but it is the thrown stick that returns.
explanation.definitionFit: A curved throwing stick designed to return to the person who throws it.

clue.text: Part of the family giving news to us

parts.note: gen is British slang for information or news

explanation.surface: A relative brings us news.
explanation.walkthrough: 'family' looks like relatives but is the biological rank: a family contains several genera.
explanation.definitionFit: In biological classification a family is divided into genera.

clue.text: Left a section without many words

parts.note: a conic is a conic section, a curve cut from a cone

explanation.surface: A portion was left out of a text with few words.
explanation.definitionFit: Laconic speech uses very few words, terse and to the point.

clue.text: Style of art in which silver's applied to new figure

indicators.note: in which means the silver goes inside the style of art

parts.note: Deco is short for Art Deco, a design style
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: An art movement in which silver leaf is laid on a fresh figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'figure' looks like a sculpted form but is the geometric shape.
explanation.definitionFit: A decagon is a plane geometric figure with ten sides.

clue.text: Composer, not one to cloy

indicators.note: not means the letter for one is removed from the composer's name

parts.note: Erik Satie was a French composer
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A musician who is never too sweet.
explanation.definitionFit: To sate is to satisfy to excess, the same sickly fullness as to cloy.

clue.text: Implores to move to London, say

indicators.note: move means the letters of implores to are shifted into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone begs another to relocate to London.
explanation.definitionFit: London is an example of a large capital city, a metropolis.
